title: Hold-Up Play (Target Man)
content: Hold-up play involves a striker receiving the ball with their back to goal and using their body strength to hold off a defender while teammates advance and support positions are established. The hold-up player is not primarily trying to turn and score — they are acting as an anchor who buys time for the team to push up the pitch and create an overload. Good hold-up play requires: physical strength and balance to hold under pressure, technical ability to protect the ball with the body, and awareness of support runners approaching. The hold-up player has several options: turn if they create separation, lay off to a supporting runner arriving from the side, or draw a foul. Most effective when the team is under pressure and needs to relieve that pressure by winning territory.
